chest.name: Bench Press
chest.description: Lie flat, grip slightly wider than shoulders. Lower the bar to mid-chest, press up explosively.

chest.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
chest.description: Set bench to 30–45°. Press dumbbells from shoulder level until arms are extended overhead.

chest.name: Cable Fly
chest.description: Stand between cables set at shoulder height. Bring handles together in a wide arc, squeezing the chest at the midline.

chest.name: Chest Dip
chest.description: Lean forward 20–30° to bias the chest. Lower until shoulders are below elbows, then push up.

chest.name: Push-Up
chest.description: Hands shoulder-width apart. Lower chest to the floor while keeping hips level, then press back up.

shoulders.name: Overhead Press
shoulders.description: Press a barbell or dumbbells from shoulder height to full lockout overhead. Brace your core throughout.

shoulders.name: Lateral Raise
shoulders.description: Hold dumbbells at your sides. Raise them out to 90° with a slight forward lean — lead with elbows, not wrists.

shoulders.name: Face Pull
shoulders.description: Set cable at forehead height, use rope attachment. Pull toward your face, elbows flaring high, and externally rotate at the end.

shoulders.name: Arnold Press
shoulders.description: Start with palms facing you at chin height. Rotate hands outward as you press overhead, reversing on the way down.

shoulders.name: Rear Delt Fly
shoulders.description: Bent over or lying face-down on incline bench. Raise dumbbells out to the sides keeping arms nearly straight.

biceps.name: Barbell Curl
biceps.description: Stand upright. Curl the bar from full extension to shoulder height without swinging your elbows forward.

biceps.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
biceps.description: Set bench to 60°. Let arms hang fully extended. Curl without letting the upper arm drift forward — full stretch at the bottom.

biceps.name: Hammer Curl
biceps.description: Neutral grip (thumbs up). Curl to shoulder height. Targets the brachialis and brachioradialis as well.

biceps.name: Concentration Curl
biceps.description: Seated, elbow braced against inner thigh. Curl one dumbbell in full isolation — slow and controlled.

biceps.name: Cable Curl
biceps.description: Cable keeps tension through the entire arc, including at the top where dumbbells lose it. Great finisher.

triceps.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
triceps.description: Grip the bar at shoulder width. Lower to lower chest and press, keeping elbows tucked close to the torso.

triceps.name: Skull Crusher
triceps.description: Lie flat with an EZ-bar. Lower bar toward forehead by bending only at the elbow, then extend back to start.

triceps.name: Triceps Pushdown
triceps.description: Cable set high, rope or bar attachment. Drive handles down until elbows are fully extended. Keep upper arms fixed.

triceps.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
triceps.description: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands. Lower behind head until elbows are at 90°, then extend.

triceps.name: Triceps Dip
triceps.description: Stay upright (torso vertical) to keep emphasis on the triceps instead of the chest. Full lockout at the top.

forearms.name: Wrist Curl
forearms.description: Seated with forearms on thighs, palms up. Curl wrists upward through full range of motion.

forearms.name: Reverse Curl
forearms.description: Overhand grip on a barbell or cable. Curl to shoulder height — heavily loads the brachioradialis and extensors.

forearms.name: Farmer's Walk
forearms.description: Grip heavy dumbbells or trap bar and walk for distance. Simple, brutal, highly effective for grip strength.

forearms.name: Plate Pinch
forearms.description: Pinch two plates together (smooth sides out) and hold at your side. Time each hold.

forearms.name: Dead Hang
forearms.description: Hang from a pull-up bar in full extension. Develops grip endurance and decompresses the spine.

abs.name: Plank
abs.description: Forearms on floor, body in a straight line from head to heels. Squeeze glutes and breathe steadily.

abs.name: Cable Crunch
abs.description: Kneeling at high cable, rope at neck. Crunch elbows toward knees — isolates the rectus abdominis under load.

abs.name: Hanging Leg Raise
abs.description: Hang from bar. Raise straight legs to 90° (or knees to chest for regression). Control the descent.

abs.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
abs.description: Kneel with hands on the wheel. Roll out until hips are about to drop, pull back using your core — not your hips.

abs.name: Weighted Sit-Up
abs.description: Hold a plate across your chest or behind your head. Full range of motion — shoulders off the floor at the bottom.

obliques.name: Russian Twist
obliques.description: Seated, feet elevated or on floor. Rotate a weight from side to side — keep back straight, not rounded.

obliques.name: Side Plank
obliques.description: Forearm or straight arm. Hips up in line with body. Add hip dips for extra range.

obliques.name: Cable Woodchop
obliques.description: Pull cable from high to low (or low to high). Rotate through the torso — don't just use arms.

obliques.name: Bicycle Crunch
obliques.description: Alternate bringing opposite elbow to knee in a slow, controlled pedalling motion. No neck pulling.

obliques.name: Pallof Press
obliques.description: Stand perpendicular to cable. Press handle straight out and hold — resists rotation, building anti-rotational strength.

serratus.name: Serratus Punch
serratus.description: Lie on bench or floor holding a dumbbell. Arm fully extended, 'punch' the ceiling by protracting the shoulder blade.

serratus.name: Push-Up Plus
serratus.description: At the top of a push-up, continue pushing into the floor to round the upper back (protract scapulae). Builds the serratus.

serratus.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
serratus.description: Lean slightly forward at a high cable. Pull the bar to your hips with straight arms — the lat and serratus both fire.

serratus.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
serratus.description: During the rollout, the serratus has to protract and upwardly rotate the scapula to maintain form.

serratus.name: Wall Slide
serratus.description: Stand facing wall with forearms flat on it. Slide arms up while pushing into the wall — great for serratus activation.

traps.name: Barbell Shrug
traps.description: Hold a heavy barbell at arm's length. Shrug straight up (not rolling) as high as possible. Pause at the top.

traps.name: Rack Pull
traps.description: Set pins just below knee. Pull like a deadlift — the upper traps work hard to keep the bar close and retract the scapulae.

traps.name: Face Pull
traps.description: High cable with rope. Pull to forehead with elbows high — directly targets the mid and upper traps along with the rear delts.

traps.name: Upright Row
traps.description: Barbell or cable, narrow grip. Pull to chin level, leading with elbows. Wide grip biases the upper traps.

traps.name: Dumbbell Shrug
traps.description: Same mechanic as barbell shrug but allows a fuller range of motion and independent movement of each side.

lats.name: Pull-Up
lats.description: Dead hang, overhand grip. Pull until chin clears the bar — focus on driving elbows down toward your hips.

lats.name: Lat Pulldown
lats.description: Wide overhand grip. Pull bar to upper chest, leaning back slightly. Feel the lats stretch fully at the top.

lats.name: Bent-Over Row
lats.description: Hinge to ~45°, overhand or underhand grip. Pull bar to lower chest/upper abdomen. Row through your elbows, not hands.

lats.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
lats.description: Brace on bench. Pull dumbbell to hip — elbow past your torso at the top. Allows heavier loading and longer range.

lats.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
lats.description: High cable, arms straight. Pull bar down to hips — isolates the lat without biceps involvement.

lower-back.name: Deadlift
lower-back.description: Hinge at the hips, neutral spine, bar close. Drive through the floor and lock out hips at the top. The king of posterior chain lifts.

lower-back.name: Romanian Deadlift
lower-back.description: Hinge with soft knees, bar dragging down the legs. Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive hips forward.

lower-back.name: Good Morning
lower-back.description: Bar on traps, hinge forward keeping the back flat until torso is near horizontal. Teaches the hip hinge pattern safely.

lower-back.name: Hyperextension
lower-back.description: On a GHD or back extension bench. Lower until back is parallel to floor, then raise back to neutral — don't hyperextend at the top.

lower-back.name: Bird Dog
lower-back.description: On hands and knees. Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously. Builds spinal stability and erector endurance.

glutes.name: Hip Thrust
glutes.description: Upper back on bench, barbell across hips. Drive hips to full extension — squeeze hard at the top for 1 second.

glutes.name: Barbell Squat
glutes.description: High or low bar back squat. Drive knees out and break parallel for maximum glute recruitment.

glutes.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
glutes.description: Rear foot elevated, front foot far forward. Drop the hips straight down — one of the best single-leg glute exercises.

glutes.name: Glute Bridge
glutes.description: Lie on floor, feet flat. Drive hips to full extension — a lighter version of the hip thrust, great for activation warm-ups.

glutes.name: Cable Kickback
glutes.description: Attach ankle strap to low cable. Kick straight back until hip is fully extended. Keep the torso steady.

quads.name: Barbell Squat
quads.description: Quad emphasis: higher bar position, narrower stance, more forward knee travel over the toes.

quads.name: Leg Press
quads.description: Feet low and narrow on the platform to maximize quad activation. Control the descent — don't lock out at the top.

quads.name: Hack Squat
quads.description: Machine or barbell behind heels. Deep range of motion with forward knee travel — great for lower quad sweep.

quads.name: Lunge
quads.description: Step forward into a 90° bend. Keep the torso upright to keep tension on the lead quad.

quads.name: Leg Extension
quads.description: Machine isolation for the quads. Squeeze hard at the top. Good as a finisher after compounds.

hamstrings.name: Romanian Deadlift
hamstrings.description: Hinge at the hip with slight knee bend. Bar stays close to the legs. Stretch hamstrings at the bottom, squeeze glutes on the way up.

hamstrings.name: Leg Curl
hamstrings.description: Seated or lying machine. Full stretch at the top, curl to maximum knee flexion. Slow on the way back down.

hamstrings.name: Nordic Curl
hamstrings.description: Anchor feet, lower yourself to the floor under control using only hamstring eccentric strength. One of the hardest bodyweight exercises.

hamstrings.name: Good Morning
hamstrings.description: Bar on traps, hinge with soft knees. Hamstrings load heavily during the stretch phase of the movement.

hamstrings.name: Glute-Ham Raise
hamstrings.description: GHD machine. Lower with straight body, then curl yourself back up using the hamstrings. Brutal but highly effective.

calves.name: Standing Calf Raise
calves.description: Full range of motion — deep stretch at the bottom, pause at the top. Targets the gastrocnemius.

calves.name: Seated Calf Raise
calves.description: With knees bent, the gastrocnemius is slackened, so this isolates the soleus. Use moderate weight and high reps.

calves.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
calves.description: Feet on the bottom edge of the leg press plate. Push through the ball of the foot through full range of motion.

calves.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
calves.description: Hold one dumbbell for resistance. Single-leg version exposes and corrects strength imbalances between sides.

calves.name: Jump Rope
calves.description: Stay on the balls of your feet. Builds calf endurance and explosive elasticity — underrated conditioning tool.

hip-flexors.name: Hanging Knee Raise
hip-flexors.description: Hang from bar. Drive knees up toward chest. Control the descent to keep hip flexors under tension.

hip-flexors.name: Cable Hip Flexion
hip-flexors.description: Ankle strap on low cable. Drive knee up to waist height against resistance. Slow and controlled.

hip-flexors.name: Mountain Climber
hip-flexors.description: In push-up position. Alternate driving knees toward chest in a running motion. Also builds core and cardio.

hip-flexors.name: Psoas March
hip-flexors.description: Lying on floor with lower back pressed down. Alternate lifting one knee toward your chest in a slow, controlled march.

hip-flexors.name: Reverse Crunch
hip-flexors.description: Lie flat, bring knees to chest by tilting the pelvis — works the lower abs and hip flexors together.

adductors.name: Sumo Squat
adductors.description: Wide stance, toes pointed out at 45°. The wide base puts significant tension on the inner thighs throughout.

adductors.name: Cable Hip Adduction
adductors.description: Ankle strap on low cable. Stand sideways, pull the working leg across the body. Control the return.

adductors.name: Copenhagen Plank
adductors.description: Side plank with top foot on a bench and bottom leg adducting up to meet it. Excellent adductor strength builder.

adductors.name: Lateral Lunge
adductors.description: Step wide to the side, bending one knee while the other leg stays straight. Great stretch and load on the adductors.

adductors.name: Adductor Machine
adductors.description: Inner thigh machine. Work through full range of motion and squeeze at the closed position.

neck.name: Chin Tuck
neck.description: Standing or seated. Gently retract your chin straight back (not down). Holds 3 s each. Strengthens deep neck flexors.

neck.name: Plate Neck Curl
neck.description: Lie face-up, plate on forehead with a towel. Curl head toward chest slowly. Builds neck flexors.

neck.name: Neck Extension
neck.description: Lie face-down, plate on back of head with a towel. Extend head up and back. Works the neck extensors and upper traps.

neck.name: Lateral Neck Flexion
neck.description: Tilt head toward shoulder against manual resistance or a light band. Develops lateral neck stability.

neck.name: Resistance Band Neck Press
neck.description: Band around head, standing. Push head forward, back, and laterally against band resistance — 360° neck development.

tibialis.name: Toe Raise
tibialis.description: Stand with heels on a step or flat floor. Raise toes as high as possible, hold 1 s, lower. Often neglected and easy to fix.

tibialis.name: Tibialis Raise (seated)
tibialis.description: Sit on a bench, heels on the floor. Raise toes up against gravity or a light band — great for runners and shin splint prevention.

tibialis.name: Heel Walk
tibialis.description: Walk on heels only — toes raised the whole time. Builds tibialis anterior endurance.

tibialis.name: Band Dorsiflexion
tibialis.description: Sit with a band around the top of the foot. Pull toes toward shin against resistance. Seated machine version is also great.
